source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting failed electrical appliance safety checks

1. Start with the test records.
2.
completion:
Record the date and time of the failed safety check.
3. Identify the appliance by type, make, model, and serial number.
4. List the specific safety checks conducted and their corresponding outcomes.
5. Record any visible damage or defects on the appliance.
6. Document the exact details of the failure: was it a pass/fail result from a testing device, a visual observation of irregularities, or some other method of diagnosis?
7. If using testing tools, note their calibration and last maintenance check dates.
8. Include measurements or readings if relevant (e.g., Earth Resistance, Insulation Resistance).
9. Note any error codes or warnings displayed on the appliance.
10. Check if power supply issues contributed to the failure.
11. Mention if the appliance had any reported issues or faults before the checks.
12. Provide a description of the circumstances under which the appliance was working before the safety check.
13. Capture relevant environmental conditions during the test
